Dalaran (/ˈdɑːləˌrɔːn/ DAHL-ə-RAWN), also City of Dalaran and Dalaran City, was the capital of the magocratic nation of the same name. Founded as a city-state by magi of the Arathorian Empire after the Troll Wars, it was ruled by the Kirin Tor, an elite cadre of the most powerful wizards in the known world, under the leadership of the Council of Six. Originally located near the southern coast of Lordamere Lake in Lordaeron, Dalaran was magically lifted and moved to Northrend at the time of the Nexus War and the war against the Lich King, until it was teleported to the Broken Isles during the third invasion of the Burning Legion. The Violet Citadel, the city's inner fortress described as a sanctum and haven for mages, served as the focal point for magi and the study of the arcane throughout human history. The city of Dalaran had the greatest concentration of magic in the world, other than the lands of Quel'Thalas, and was defended by some of the most powerful magi in Azeroth. The Kirin Tor Guardians patrolled and protected the surface of Dalaran, while the Underbelly Guard were the guardians of the Underbelly, the sewer system beneath the capital.
By the time of the Third War, Dalaran was home to many of the greatest sorcerers of the time, while most contemporary human and high elven mages of Quel'Thalas bowed to both the sovereignty of the Kirin Tor. However, the Siege of Dalaran by the Scourge forced the Dalaranian people to flee their kingdom, while the Kirin Tor's leadership and its surviving members were scattered after Archimonde destroyed the city. In the aftermath of the Third War, the survivors returned to rebuild the ruins of Dalaran and created a vast, magical dome around the heart of their city. After Dalaran was restored to its former glory, the Kirin Tor magically floated the city so that no ground assault by the undead could ever reach them again. The nation since became one of the foremost forces standing against the threats posed to Azeroth's survival, with Dalaran serving as a neutral ground where the heroes of every kingdom could join together against their mutual foe; a place where all were welcome, so long as they behaved themselves.
After Dalaran was teleported above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar, Xal'atath unleashed the nerubians of Azj-Kahet upon the city. The Harbinger of the Void then siphoned Dalaran's power into the Dark Heart from the Violet Citadel and ultimately used the artifact to destroy the city in an explosion. Its remains can be found across the shores of the Tranquil Strand on the Isle of Dorn.

Its remains can be found across the shores of the [[Tranquil Strand]] on the Isle of Dorn. {{OTOC|400|302}} ==History== {{Main|Dalaran (kingdom)#History}} ==In-game evolution== ===Classic=== {{wow-section}} [[File:Dalaran.jpg|thumb|Dalaran as seen in original ''[[World of Warcraft]]''.]] Dalaran was originally "hidden" behind an impassible magic dome in the [[Alterac Mountains]]. In truth, the area behind the dome was empty. With {{g|wotlk}}, the area was replaced with the [[Dalaran Crater]] since the city had then been added in [[Northrend]]. ===Wrath of the Lich King=== {{wotlk-section}} [[File:Dalaran Wrath of the Lich King.jpg|thumb|The city of Dalaran in {{g|wotlk}}.]] In {{g|wotlk}}, Dalaran acts as the shared-faction [[sanctuary]] city and can be accessed via the [[Teleport to Dalaran Crystal|teleport crystal]] in [[Violet Stand]] or through flight. There is a portal trainer at the [[Violet Gate]], but also an arena master and battlemasters in the [[Underbelly]] sewer system. Like the [[Stormwind Stockade]] and [[Ragefire Chasm]], Dalaran has its own instance within the city: the [[Violet Hold (instance)|Violet Hold]]. The city contains areas that are faction-specific in the same manner as Shattrath City is divided amongst the [[Aldor]] and [[Scryers]]. Certain parts of the city can only be reached by Alliance players ([[Silver Enclave]]) while others are strictly for Horde use ([[Sunreaver's Sanctuary]]). The majority of the city remains neutral. [[Portal]]s are located within the Alliance and Horde districts of the city, connecting to the factions' main [[Capital City|capital city]]. When first added there were originally no class trainers - with the notable exception of [[mage trainer]]s, given the city's history. Dalaran was also originally a [[no-fly zone]], dismounting flying characters when approaching the city's rooftops. [[Krasus' Landing]] was an exception, to serve as a landing area for [[flight path]]s. ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}} The portals to the faction major cities were removed in [[patch 4.0.3a]] and replaced by class trainers.[[Patch 4.0.3a (world changes)#Dalaran]] However, the portals to [[Stormwind City]] and [[Orgrimmar]] were restored in [[patch 4.1.0]]. The formerly engineering-only auctioneers — [[Brassbolt Mechawrench|Steam-Powered Auctioneer]] in [[Silver Enclave]] and [[Reginald Arcfire|Steam-Powered Auctioneer]] in [[Sunreaver's Sanctuary]] — now serve anyone and flying is allowed in the capital. ===Mists of Pandaria=== {{mop-section}} During the [[Purge of Dalaran]] in {{Expac|Mists of Pandaria}}, the city had already left Northrend and was in motion.[http://www.vanion.eu/news/update-barlow-im-interview-mit-dave-kosak-lead-quest-designer-von-wow-3961 Vanion's interview with Dave Kosak] - "So, in present-day, Dalaran is in motion and we don't say where and we are not sure if we show it in-game somewhere else. Yet we have not decided."[https://web.archive.org/web/20180523124457/https:/twitter.com/DaveKosak/status/279439327535194112 Dave Kosak on Twitter] However, [[#Notes and trivia|for game purposes]], Dalaran remains unchanged after the questline is completed. ===Legion=== {{legion-section}} [[File:Dalaran - Legion Invasion.jpg|thumb|Dalaran attacked by the [[Burning Legion|Legion]].]] During the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]], Dalaran was moved above [[Karazhan]] in [[Deadwind Pass]] to protect the [[Eastern Kingdoms]].[[Calling of the Council]][[Anomalous Anomalies]][[In the Blink of an Eye]] It was then teleported to the [[Broken Isles]] where it served as the capital city for [[adventurer]]s. During the [[Assault on Broken Shore]], [[Kil'jaeden]] sent Legion ships to destroy the city, but they were repelled by the Azeroth allied forces.[[Assault on Broken Shore (quest)]] The city's layout was overhauled for ''[[World of Warcraft: Legion|Legion]]'' with notably the [[Underbelly]] being expanded and the center of the city becoming a portal hub.{{ref web|url=http://www.mmo-champion.com/content/5077-Dev-Interviews-Rogue-Order-Hall-Blue-Posts-Warcraft-Movie-Prop-Contest-DLC-500|title=Dev Interviews, Rogue Order Hall, Blue Posts, Warcraft Movie Prop Contest, DLC #500|date=2015-08-11}} The portals were then largely removed. ===The War Within=== {{tww-section}} After Dalaran was moved above the [[Isle of Dorn]] in [[Khaz Algar]], [[Xal'atath]] unleashed the [[nerubian]]s of [[Azj-Kahet]] upon the city.[[To Khaz Algar!]] While the [[Kirin Tor]] defended the city alongside the [[Silver Covenant]] and [[Sunreavers]], Xal'atath siphoned Dalaran's power into the [[Dark Heart]] from the [[Violet Citadel]] and ultimately used the artifact to defeat [[Khadgar]] and destroy the city.[[Departure]] The remaining pieces of Dalaran later landed on the [[Tranquil Strand]] and [[Oztan Isle]] below, along with the teleported survivors.[[Violent Impact]] On the [[Isle of Dorn]], [[Aethas Sunreaver]] led the effort to cleanse the excess arcane energy from the city's ruins and gave a send-off to the city of magic with assistance from the [[Kirin Tor]], [[Sunreavers]], and [[Silver Covenant]] coming to terms that the city will never be rebuilt as the Kirin Tor must move away from "floating cities".[[Farewell, City of Magic]] When the champions of [[Azeroth]] battled [[Dimensius]] within the [[Dark Heart]], they saw the remains of the city absorbed by the relic.[[Manaforge Omega]] File:Dalaran nerubian invasion.jpg|Dalaran invaded by the [[nerubian]]s of [[Azj-Kahet]]. Led by {{NPC||Vereesa Windrunner||Ranger-General Vereesa Windrunner|icon=Vereesa}}. *{{Horde}} [[File:Sunreaver Tabard.jpg|16x16px]] [[Sunreavers]] - Representatives of the [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|kingdom of Quel'Thalas]] and the Horde in Dalaran. Led by {{NPC||Aethas Sunreaver||Archmage Aethas Sunreaver|icon=Aethas}}. ==Notable residents== {{Main|Dalaran NPCs|Dalaran (Northrend) NPCs}} ==Getting there== ==={{wotlk-inline}} Getting to Dalaran in Northrend=== Dalaran is located in the north-central region of the continent of [[Northrend]], floating above the western side of [[Crystalsong Forest]]. Players can reach it quickly by using the portal in their faction's [[portal room]] to "Dalaran, Crystalsong Forest". [[Boats|Ships]]The [[Cataclysm travel guide]] provides more information on the ship and zeppelin routes to [[Northrend]], item and quest portals to Dalaran, and suggests ways higher level players can shorten travel times between Dalaran and their faction capitals. and [[zeppelin]]s departing from [[Stormwind]] and [[Orgrimmar]] provide traditional means of access to Northrend from [[Kalimdor]] and the [[Eastern Kingdoms]]. ;Traveling from within [[Northrend]] *The quest [[The Magical Kingdom of Dalaran]] will cause various [[Kirin Tor]] NPCs to provide a teleport to Dalaran until you complete the quest. As long as it remains uncompleted, players can speak to the NPC to travel quickly from [[The Magical Kingdom of Dalaran#Quest guide|various Northrend zones]] to Dalaran. *A set of crystals ([[Teleport to Violet Stand Crystal]] and [[Teleport to Dalaran Crystal]]) can be used to teleport there. The [[Teleport to Violet Stand Crystal]] must be used first by doing [[Learning to Leave and Return: the Magical Way]] from the portal trainer [[Archmage Celindra]], so you must first reach Dalaran via another method. **This causes [[The Magical Kingdom of Dalaran]] to become unavailable. *If your faction has won the previous [[Wintergrasp]] battle, you can take the [[Wintergrasp]] portal to the [[Violet Citadel]]. The portal is inside the [[Wintergrasp Fortress]]. **A separate guide, [[Getting to Wintergrasp and Dalaran]], provides a few ways to get to Wintergrasp. *A Dalaran portal appears after completing the [[Trial of the Crusader]]. *The flight master at [[Krasus' Landing]] in Dalaran is learned automatically by all characters, allowing players to take a [[flight path]] there. *Players who know [[Riding#Skill levels|expert riding]] can fly directly to Dalaran with a flying [[mount]]. ;Traveling from anywhere *Mages can learn a portal to Dalaran from the [[portal trainer]]. Mages can teleport themselves, or provide a portal for others. *A set of [[Kirin Tor rings]] are available to characters that are high enough level. Any of these rings can teleport the character to Dalaran on use. *The [[Argent Crusader's Tabard]] teleports the player to the [[Argent Tournament Grounds]], a short distance from Dalaran. ==={{legion-inline}} Getting to Dalaran in the Broken Isles=== All players arrive in Dalaran over the Broken Isles on the quest [[In the Blink of an Eye]] and receive a [[Dalaran Hearthstone]], allowing them to teleport to Dalaran once every 20 minutes. Characters who have the [[toy box|toy]] but have not visited Broken Isles Dalaran need to travel there once. Completing the quest, or speaking to [[Amisi Azuregaze]] in the [[Legerdemain Lounge]] to receive another Dalaran Hearthstone, will enable the toy's use. Each faction's [[portal room]] has a portal to [[Azsuna]], where the player can then fly to Dalaran on a flying mount. Mages can learn a portal to Dalaran over the Broken Isles from a portal trainer, allowing them to teleport other players there. ==Leaving Dalaran== *Talking to [[Archmage Celindra|Portal Trainer Celindra]] to do [[Learning to Leave and Return: the Magical Way]] to enable the [[Teleport to Violet Stand Crystal]] which teleports to [[Violet Stand]] below Dalaran. *Players can pay to fly from the Dalaran Flight master in [[Krasus' Landing]], to nearby flight masters via a [[Flight Path|flight path]]. *Jumping off the edge of the city or from the sewer tunnel in the [[Underbelly]], though this may result in death without a way to slow the character's descent. *Characters with [[Riding#Skill levels|expert riding]] can depart with a flying [[mount]]. =={{wotlk-inline}} Travel connections in Northrend== [[File:Dalaran City.jpg|thumb|Dalaran city as seen from above in [[Northrend]].]] ===Flight=== ;{{Neutral}} [[Ebon Watch]], [[Zul'Drak]] ;{{Neutral}} [[Moa'ki Harbor]], [[Dragonblight]] ;{{Neutral}} [[Wyrmrest Temple]], [[Dragonblight]] ;{{Neutral}} [[Argent Tournament Grounds]], [[Icecrown]] ;{{Neutral}} [[Argent Vanguard]], [[Icecrown]] ;{{Alliance}} [[Fordragon Hold]], [[Dragonblight]] ;{{Horde}} [[Kor'kron Vanguard]], [[Dragonblight]] ===Portals=== When ''Wrath of the Lich King'' went live, Dalaran supplanted [[Shattrath City]] as the major hub for player activity, due to easy access to the capital cities in the southern continents, to Outland via Shattrath, and to the high-level content in Northrend. to the left of the entrance of [[A Hero's Welcome]]. Although they are both near the faction-controlled areas, they are available to both the Alliance and the Horde. *The well near the [[Magus Commerce Exchange]] is an entrance to the Underbelly, when you jump into it you arrive randomly at one of four possible sites in the Underbelly. Jumping down does not cause fall damage. *All profession trainers (except [[Fishing]], [[Cooking]] and [[Archaeology]]) are located in the [[Magus Commerce Exchange]]. *All mage trainers are located in the [[Violet Gate]]. ==Film universe== {{movie-section}} {{Main|Dalaran (kingdom)#Film universe}} ==In Hearthstone== {{HS-section}} In ''[[Hearthstone (game)|Hearthstone]]'', Dalaran is the major setting of {{HS|the Great Dalaran Heist}} expansion, being invaded by the {{HS|League of E.V.I.L.}}. The Bank of Dalaran (or Dalaran Bank), the Violet Hold, streets of Dalaran, the Underbelly, and Kirin Tor Citadel are areas of battle. At the end of the heist, the League steals the entire city, flying it to [[Uldum]] to set up the {{HS|Saviors of Uldum}} expansion. ==Notes and trivia== [[File:Dalaran early layout concept.jpg|thumb|An early layout concept by [[Cory Stockton]].{{tw|https://web.archive.org/web/20210302195830/https://twitter.com/mumper/status/439280468664410112|2014-02-07|Mumper|My 1st pass layout of Dalaran for WotLK. Made a few changes along the way, but it came out pretty damn close.}}]] ;Lore *Dalaran has a cemetery.[[Waking the Dead]] *The city's foundation has cracks.[[Glowing Foundations]] *The Underbelly has a severe rodent problem.[[Pesky Pest Problem]] *The tallest spire in Dalaran City is called Dalaran Spire.[https://www.wowhead.com/spell=235124/portal-dalaran-spire Wowhead] One of the spires [[Malfunctioning Spire|malfunctioned]] and turned into a [[crystal elemental]] after the city's crash. The [[nerubian spiderlord]] [[Anub'esska]] was known as [[:the Spirebreaker]] for her actions against the city. *Among the ornate spires and enchanted streets of Dalaran, the great [[Violet Hold]] stands as a testament to the glory of the city's rulers.{{ref web |url=http://www.worldofwarcraft.com/info/dungeons/wrath-violet-hold.xml |title=The Violet Hold |accessdate=2009-03-17 |format=HTML |work = Wrath Dungeons |publisher = [[Blizzard Entertainment Inc.]] |language = English}} *A group of [[high elf]] [[engineer]]s helped build Dalaran's original defenses. These engineers later ended up as [[Blood elf|blood elves]] in [[Kael'thas Sunstrider]]'s [[Sunfury|army]].[[The Crossing (WC3 BloodElf)]] **The city is protected by defensive shields based on Antonidas' earlier version of a magical field that destroyed any undead that touched it during the Third War.The Archmage Antonidas - Part III **Dalaran had no trained [[militia]] by the time of the [[Third War]].''[[Arthas: Rise of the Lich King]]'', chapter 20 *Dalaran used phosphorescent crystals, which beamed with a steady, constant glow, though a research spoke of reflective mirrors, elemental spirits bound within lanterns, and in one case, huge captive fireflies.''[[The Last Guardian]]'', chapter 1 *The city's libraries record up to twenty centuries of [[human]] history, though the earliest histories are wrapped in legends.''[[The Last Guardian]]'', chapter 8 *Dalaran has magic [[school|schools]] where young mages and schoolchildren are educated and trained in the use of magic.[[STAY OUT!!!]][[The Old Wizard's Almanac]] *Dalaran has an [[orphanage]], where [[Alodi]] was raised.[[Archive of the Tirisgarde#Ebonchill, Greatstaff of Alodi]] It was originally supposed to appear in-game, at the location of the present-day [[Sisters Sorcerous]]'s shop.[[:File:Dalaran early layout concept.jpg]] *The [[Dalaranium]] is a [[Rare Metal|rare metal]], named after the city of Dalaran, that can be found in trash heaps of [[Mechagon Island]].[[One Gnome's Trash]] *Grasses of the [[Alterac Mountains]] are still growing around the outskirts of the floating city. They are hearty and impart a strong, earthy flavor to hot tea.[[The Fate of Apprentice Argoly]] ;Gameplay *[[Jaina's Locket]] and the [[Ring of the Kirin Tor]] are permanent teleport items to the Northrend version of Dalaran. *While in Dalaran, you may randomly get [[The Mischief Maker|Manabonked]] by [[Minigob Manabonk]]. *When night falls, [[Windle Sparkshine]] will light most of the lamps in Dalaran, then stand outside the [[Alliance]] section of Dalaran, and will sell [[Windle's Lighter]] for 50 Silver. *Compared to other major cities, Dalaran has very many activities. Examples include /Pet'ing [[Jones]], lighting up the city with [[Windle's Lighter]], seeking [[Higher Learning]], and [[fishing]] for treasures like the [[Giant Sewer Rat]]. *Dalaran is smaller than the other major cities in the game. At the same time, it has a large number of NPCs, doodads, and objects. This accumulates a high amount of players at a small area, along with causing a player's computer to load several city details at once. Back in the day of ''WotLK'', the result was often a mediocre to a large degree of [[lag]] when the player was inside the city. The lag experienced within Dalaran was a very common topic within World of Warcraft; some players even dubbed the city "Lagaran" because of it. It was not uncommon for a character in Dalaran to be unable to perform any action at all, use abnormally much time on simple actions such as walking, or be even repeatedly disconnected when attempting to log in if the character was located in the city. The problem was severe enough that Blizzard had to implement the [[Argent Tournament]] in [[Icecrown]] away from Dalaran, rather than in [[Crystalsong Forest]] directly underneath it as originally planned. *Since [[patch 11.0.2]], there are six separate "Dalarans" in the game (not counting [[Dalaran Crater]]), each reflecting a different period in the city's history: **the Northrend version above Crystalsong Forest. **the instance used during the [[Operation: Shieldwall]]/[[Dominance Offensive]] storyline. **the Karazhan-overwatch version that phases in after the [[Battle for the Broken Shore]]. **the ''Legion''-era Dalaran over the Broken Isles. **an instanced, NPC-free copy visible from the balcony of the [[Hall of the Guardian]]. **a partially destroyed version in the ''Intro: Visions of Azeroth'' opening questline scenario for ''[[The War Within]]'', after which Dalaran is destroyed by Xal'atath. *Dalaran can be seen in the [[End Time]] dungeon, but not in the [[Dragon Soul]] raid. **The version of Dalaran seen in the [[patch 5.1]] storylines (the [[Operation: Shieldwall]] and [[Dominance Offensive]] quest chains) is located in its own instance, similar to [[Plaguelands: The Scarlet Enclave]], rather than being a phased version of the main-world Dalaran. It uses the [[Violet Hold (instance)|Violet Hold]] loading screen rather than the Northrend one and is floating over what looks like a sea. The [[world map]] interface bar shows its location in Eastern Kingdoms. Besides the NPC changes, there is no Violet Hold instance portal in this version, flying is impossible (even at Krasus' Landing), and jumping off the Underbelly pipe kills the player before they reach the water below. **Dalaran over Karazhan, seen between completing [[The Battle for Broken Shore (quest)]] and [[In the Blink of an Eye]], is an intermediate version between the Northrend and Broken Isles Dalarans. The [[Chamber of the Guardian]] exists in this version but the teleport pad is not working; the [[Silver Enclave]] and [[Sunreaver's Sanctuary]] still have those names, rather than their new names in ''Legion'' (and both are accessible to both factions); the city is full of [[Kirin Tor Guardian]]s, and most NPCs only offer gossip text instead of their regular services. *In an interview with Jesse Cox, [[Dave Kosak]] revealed that Dalaran was planned to be in the air above the [[Siege of Orgrimmar (instance)|Siege of Orgrimmar]], but technical limitations meant they had to scrap the idea. It is possible this is related to the limitations that prevented the [[Argent Tournament]] from being placed in Crystalsong Forest.[http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=osB0_0G5N8g Warcraft Interview: Dave Kosak - 2 NERDS, 1 LORE (Patch 5.4 and beyond)] ;Other *Strangely, in-game there is no "old gate" on the side of the land mass and the other halves of the houses in Alterac Mountains aren't there either. *The decision to have Dalaran as the {{g|legion}} sanctuary resulted in mixed results among players, with some wondering why the Horde would want to return after the [[Purge of Dalaran]] and others feeling that Dalaran has left the Alliance and become neutral. *Dalaran and Dalaran Ruins are melee [[tileset]]s in ''Warcraft III'' and ''The Frozen Throne'', representing the city before and after its destruction by Archimonde. *Dalaran is probably inspired by [[wikipedia:Celephaïs|Serannian]], a pink marble city in the clouds part of [[wikipedia:H._P._Lovecraft|H.P. Lovecraft]]'s [[wikipedia:Dreamlands|Dreamlands]]. * Although the city's name is officially pronounced {{IPA|/ˈdɑːləˌrɔːn/}} {{respell|DAHL-ə-RAWN}}, some individuals—particularly among the player community, and in rare audiobook or in-game voice lines—occasionally pronounce it as {{IPA|/ˈdæl.əˌræn/}} {{respell|DAL-ə-ran}}, likely due to spelling influence or similarity to common English patterns. **This is likely an oversight, as no in-universe explanation for this discrepancy has been provided. **During ''[[The War Within]]'' expansion, during which the city was destroyed, this alternate pronunciation became more common among voiced NPCs—most notably during [[Legion: Remix]]—where several characters who had previously not used the pronunciation began to do so. ==Gallery== File:Eye of Dalaran symbol.jpg|The [[Kirin Tor]] symbol.
